notes: not an SSM, so the window check cannot reach it: delta(d)*t is fitted by profile non-linear least squares on within-well-demeaned monthly levels over the whole record, reference and extended wells together, less FE, scraped and clearfell-zone wells. Three bases used to meet in 25_03_cluster_partition.csv and they were not the same basis: the panel delta(d) is CWB-adjusted and all-season, the per-well slopes in 25_02 are RAW annual seasonal-metric OLS, and the observed column was a Script-14 cluster-CENTROID slope rather than the per-well mean. Reconciled 2026-08-19 in Script 25 v1.6.0: the decomposition is now computed against observed_balanced_annual_mean_mm_yr, the slope of the annual cross-well mean of the seasonal metric over the same well-set as 25_02, which is one OLS on one annual series rather than an average of per-well fits taken over different record windows. The basis is named in the file by the decomposition_basis column; the centroid slope and the per-well mean are retained beside it as context and are no longer subtracted from. The panel constant is carried as far_field_offset_mm_yr beside climate_cwb_mm_yr, the CWB covariate trend contribution. Within any one fitting window the two ARE separately identified - the constant's variance inflation factor against the covariate is 1.01 - so the file carries both rather than their sum. What is not stable is the SPLIT ACROSS WINDOWS: sliding a fixed-length window along the record, the constant and the covariate's trend contribution correlate at -0.60 to -0.82, and the constant's spread reaches 7 to 16 times its own within-window standard error. Their sum is far better determined than either part, which is why no far-field rate is quoted anywhere in this work (D-044 as amended 2026-08-21; the earlier wording here said the two were not separately identified, which answered a different question from the one the VIF measures). 25_10_record_length_composition.csv records the record-length composition that made the old per-well mean carry a far-field decline the panel constant does not
